## Decision framing

::: {.kicker}
AWS vs local
:::

::: {.rule}
:::

:::: {.grid-2}
::: {.card .pale-green}
::: {.label .green}
Local strengths
:::

- Closest match to the current framework
- We do this already for IRIS
- We can optimize for the hardware we have
- Lower recurring cost if utilization stays steady
:::

::: {.card .pale-blue}
::: {.label .blue}
AWS strengths
:::

- Elastic reprocessing bursts
- Managed services and easier off-site durability
  - "Less" IT work
- Pay-for-use cost "can" make costs known upfront
- Possible path for larger-scale L3 or campaign reprocessing
:::
::::


::: {.banner}
PUNCH did not have any numbers (lost in email transition) but said as soon as you worked out the egress cost, it was the bulk of the cost
:::

:::: {.grid-2 .compact}
::: {.card}
::: {.label .blue}
Data and pricing
:::

- Oregon (us-west-2) On-Demand list prices from AWS price files (16-22 Sep 2026); no Savings Plans, tax or support plan
- 389 GB ({{< var cost.l0_gib >}} GiB) of L0; L1 {{< var cost.l1_gib >}} GiB and L2 {{< var cost.l2_gib >}} GiB from local benchmark size ratios
- About {{< var cost.l0_files >}} L0 files (~2-3 MB each)
- Storage is the monthly price ÷ 30; compute runs the full 24 h
- L2 downloaded once, straight from S3, at $0.09/GB; the free 100 GB assumed used up (else $9 less)
- L3 about {{< var cost.l3_gib >}} GiB (one merged file, measured on a simulated flare), uploaded back to S3 (free); the L3 machine is not priced
:::

::: {.card}
::: {.label .amber}
Per line item
:::

- EC2: one `m7i.2xlarge` at {{< var cost.ec2_rate >}}/h, Dagster on the same host, 8 vCPUs (Intel's 4th Generation Xeon - Sapphire Rapids) and 32 GiB of memory
- RDS: `db.m7g.large` Multi-AZ at {{< var cost.rds_rate >}}/h, plus 100 GiB of gp3
- EC2 disk: 1 TiB of gp3 (132 GiB root, Docker and logs + ~890 GiB of files in progress); L1 is temporary, local files deleted once L2 is in S3
- Last bar: one day of L0, L2 and L3 in S3 Standard ({{< var cost.day_s3 >}}), {{< var cost.day_puts >}} PUTs + {{< var cost.day_gets >}} GETs ({{< var cost.day_req >}}), NAT + one public IPv4 ({{< var cost.day_nat >}}), database and disk backups ({{< var cost.day_backups >}}), logs and secrets ({{< var cost.day_logs >}})
- Not included: CloudWatch, LIST/retry/KMS requests, cross-Region copies, extra downloads; storage tiers; egress to NASA/SDAC
:::
::::

## Why a month costs more than 30 days

::: {.kicker}
AWS vs local
:::

::: {.rule}
:::

|                                          |           Low |          High | What decides it                                          |
| ---------------------------------------- | ------------: | ------------: | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| Always on: EC2, RDS, NAT, requests, logs | {{< var cost.m_always >}} | {{< var cost.m_always >}} | Instance sizes; Multi-AZ database |
| EC2 disk, kept at 1 TiB                  | {{< var cost.m_ebs >}} | {{< var cost.m_ebs >}} | Pipeline must delete local files after upload (not built) |
| S3 storage                               | {{< var cost.m_s3_lo >}} | {{< var cost.m_s3_hi >}} | Whether L2 and L3 are kept after 90 days |
| Egress (data leaving AWS)                | {{< var cost.m_eg_lo >}} | {{< var cost.m_eg_hi >}} | What is downloaded, and how often |
| **Total per month**                      | **{{< var cost.m_lo >}}** | **{{< var cost.m_hi >}}** | |

- **S3 storage grows with the mission:** one day stores a single day of L0, L2 and L3 ({{< var cost.day_s3 >}}).
  By the end of year 1 you pay for a year of L0 in Glacier, 90 days of L2 and L3 in S3 Standard, and, optionally, older L2 and L3 in Glacier Instant Retrieval.
  Moving about {{< var cost.l0_files >}} L0 files a day into Glacier adds {{< var cost.m_l0_moves >}} a month
- **Egress depends on who downloads what:** the low end ({{< var cost.m_eg_lo >}}) is 30 daily L2 downloads, a little cheaper because the first 100 GB a month are free.
  The high end adds the L0 archive copy, the NASA copy and scientists downloading {{< var cost.share_hi >}} of L2 and L3
- **Hourly items barely change:** AWS bills a month as 730 hours, not 720

## What leaves AWS each month

::: {.kicker}
AWS vs local
:::

::: {.rule}
:::

| Leaving AWS every day                  | Per month     | Cost per month |
| ------------------------------------   | --------:     | -------------: |
| L2 once, for L3 done elsewhere         | {{< var cost.eg_l2_tib >}} | {{< var cost.eg_l2 >}} |
| \+ L1 delivery (start of mission)      | {{< var cost.eg_l1_tib >}} | {{< var cost.eg_l1 >}} |
| \+ L0 copy to an archive               | {{< var cost.eg_l0_tib >}} | {{< var cost.eg_l0 >}} |
| \+ NASA copy of L2 and L3              | {{< var cost.eg_nasa_tib >}} | {{< var cost.eg_nasa >}} |
| \+ Scientists pull {{< var cost.shares >}} of L2 and L3 | {{< var cost.eg_sci_tib >}} | {{< var cost.eg_sci >}} |

Internet egress is $0.09/GB for the first 10 TB a month, then $0.085 and $0.07; the first 100 GB are free.

::: {.banner .amber}
Every extra full download of a level adds about {{< var cost.eg_extra >}} a month: who downloads what is the biggest cost question
:::

## Storage over the mission

::: {.kicker}
AWS vs local
:::

::: {.rule}
:::

:::: {.grid-2}
::: {.card .pale-blue }
::: {.label .blue}
S3: where data is kept
:::

- **L0, kept for the mission:** 30 days in S3 Standard, then Glacier Flexible Retrieval ({{< var cost.glacier_rate >}}/GB-month; bulk restores for reprocessing are free). Each year kept adds about {{< var cost.l0_growth >}} a month
- About {{< var cost.l0_files >}} L0 files a day cost {{< var cost.m_l0_moves >}} a month just to move into Glacier; bundling them into ~1 GB files removes almost all of that
- **L1:** not kept; rebuilt from L0 when needed. A temporary L1 bucket for the first months of the mission costs up to about {{< var cost.l1_90d >}} a month (90 days kept)
- **L2 + L3:** 90 days is about {{< var cost.l23_90d >}} a month; keeping them for the mission in Glacier Instant Retrieval adds about {{< var cost.l23_growth >}} a month per year
:::

::: {.card .pale-amber }
::: {.label .amber}
EC2 disk: where the pipeline works
:::

- The pipeline only works on a normal disk (EBS, attached to the EC2 instance); it can't read or write S3 directly
- Plan: fetch L0 from S3 (or read it through a mount), make L1 and L2, push L2 to S3, then delete the local files
- A 1 TiB disk ({{< var cost.m_ebs >}} a month) is then enough; this is new pipeline work
:::
::::

::: {.banner}
After year 1, S3 costs {{< var cost.s3_y1 >}} a month and grows by {{< var cost.s3_growth >}} a month for each further year
:::

## L2 → L3 on two GPUs in the cloud

::: {.kicker}
AWS vs local
:::

::: {.rule}
:::

| Two GPUs                          | Per hour | 8 h a day, per month | 24 h a day, per month |
| --------------------------------- | -------: | -------------------: | --------------------: |
| 2× T4 16 GB | {{< var cost.gpu_t4 >}} | {{< var cost.gpu_t4_8 >}} | {{< var cost.gpu_t4_24 >}} |
| 2× L4 24 GB | {{< var cost.gpu_l4 >}} | {{< var cost.gpu_l4_8 >}} | {{< var cost.gpu_l4_24 >}} |
| 2× A10G 24 GB | {{< var cost.gpu_a10g >}} | {{< var cost.gpu_a10g_8 >}} | {{< var cost.gpu_a10g_24 >}} |
| **2× A10G 24 GB, 16 vCPU / 64 GiB each (chosen for now)** | **{{< var cost.gpu_g54 >}}** | **{{< var cost.gpu_g54_8 >}}** | **{{< var cost.gpu_g54_24 >}}** |
| 2× L40S 48 GB | {{< var cost.gpu_l40s >}} | {{< var cost.gpu_l40s_8 >}} | {{< var cost.gpu_l40s_24 >}} |
| 2× H100 80 GB | {{< var cost.gpu_h100 >}} | {{< var cost.gpu_h100_8 >}} | {{< var cost.gpu_h100_24 >}} |

::: {.compact}
**Chosen for now: 2× `g5.4xlarge`.** Each has 1× NVIDIA A10G (24 GB), 16 vCPUs (AMD EPYC 7R32, 2.8 GHz), 64 GiB of RAM, a 600 GB local NVMe SSD and up to 25 Gbit/s of network. We don't know yet whether L2 → L3 needs a machine this big
:::

:::: {.grid-2}
::: {.card .pale-green }
::: {.label .green}
What it saves
:::

- No daily L2 download: {{< var cost.eg_l2 >}} a month less
- For that money, two L4 (~1/2 of a 4090) GPUs can run about {{< var cost.l4_hours >}} hours a day
- Or the chosen `g5.4xlarge` pair for about {{< var cost.l3_gpu_hours >}} hours a day
:::

::: {.card .pale-amber }
::: {.label .amber}
What it doesn't
:::

- If scientists download {{< var cost.shares >}} of L3, that egress stays: about {{< var cost.sci_l3 >}} a month
- Keep the pipeline and GPUs in the same Region: between Regions is $0.02/GB, about {{< var cost.xr_l2 >}} a month for L2 alone
- GPU hours per day and GPU memory requirements are unknown
:::
::::

## Saving on L0 → L2

::: {.kicker}
AWS vs local
:::

::: {.rule}
:::

| Per month, Oregon                                          |  Now |     After | Catch                                                        |
| ---------------------------------------------------------- | ---: | --------: | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Start workers per pass, stop after; Dagster on a `t4g.medium` | {{< var cost.sv_scale_now >}} | {{< var cost.sv_scale >}} | AWS Batch or an auto-scaling group                           |
| \+ Graviton (`m7g`) Spot workers                           | {{< var cost.sv_spot_now >}} | **{{< var cost.sv_spot >}}** | ARM build; must survive a worker being killed              |
| Lambda instead of EC2                                      | {{< var cost.sv_lambda_now >}} | {{< var cost.sv_lambda >}} | Needs direct S3 I/O and a new way to hand out work; about 4× Spot per vCPU-hour |
| 1-year Savings Plan, one machine always on                 | {{< var cost.sv_sp_now >}} | {{< var cost.sv_sp >}} | Rules out Spot and turning machines off                      |
| Database: single-zone `db.t4g.medium`                      | {{< var cost.sv_rds_now >}} | **{{< var cost.sv_rds >}}** | A 24-hour deadline can absorb an hour of downtime            |
| Drop the NAT gateway                                       | {{< var cost.sv_nat_now >}} | **{{< var cost.sv_nat >}}** | Public subnet, security groups, free S3 gateway endpoint     |

::: {.footer-note}
Ranges: 8 vCPUs scaling perfectly, to 2 workers only (12 h a day, unmeasured on AWS). Assumes AWS cores are {{< var cost.slowdown >}} slower than the benchmark desktop. Spot is AWS's typical saving ({{< var cost.spot_pct >}}) on 23 September 2026.
:::

## Saving on storage

::: {.kicker}
AWS vs local
:::

::: {.rule}
:::

| Per month, end of year 1                          | Saves             | Catch                                                          |
| ------------------------------------------------- | ----------------: | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| L0 older than 30 days in Glacier Deep Archive     | {{< var cost.sv_deep >}} | Restores take up to 48 hours and cost {{< var cost.restore_day >}} per day of L0; each extra year adds {{< var cost.l0_growth_deep >}} instead of {{< var cost.l0_growth >}} |
| Bundle L0 into ~1 GB files | {{< var cost.sv_bundle >}} | ~{{< var cost.bundles_day >}} files a day instead of {{< var cost.l0_files >}}; one exposure means fetching its bundle |
| L2 and L3 in S3 Intelligent-Tiering | {{< var cost.sv_it >}} | Moves files untouched for 30 days to a cheaper tier; no retrieval fees |
| Compress L0, L2 and L3 (compression in some form)    | unknown           | Cuts storage and egress; needs measuring on real files         |

::: {.banner .green}
These three need no pipeline redesign: about {{< var cost.sv_store3 >}} a month at year 1, growing each year
:::

## Saving on egress and L3

::: {.kicker}
AWS vs local
:::

::: {.rule}
:::

| Per month, end of year 1                                   | Saves           | Catch                                                           |
| ---------------------------------------------------------- | --------------: | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| NASA copy delivered inside AWS, same Region                | {{< var cost.sv_nasa >}} | Only if NASA takes delivery in AWS; from another Region about {{< var cost.sv_nasa_xr >}} |
| Scientists pay their downloads (Requester Pays, or AWS Open Data) | {{< var cost.sv_sci >}} at {{< var cost.share_hi >}} | They need AWS accounts; Open Data needs an application        |
| L3 in AWS on Oregon GPUs, batches on Spot | {{< var cost.eg_l2 >}} | Plus GPU hours, still unknown; save progress per row            |
| GFAT (3A) and SVD (3B) on CPU Spot; GPUs only for SDC rows | GPU hours       | How many rows reach SDC depends on the heuristic filter         |
| Download only L2 rows with signal                          | Part of {{< var cost.eg_l2 >}} | Depends on what is observed                                     |
| AWS research egress waiver                                 | Up to 15%       | Ask AWS whether SETI qualifies                                  |

::: {.banner .amber}
L3 is due in about a month, so it can run in weekly or monthly batches. <br> <br>
No redesign: {{< var cost.now_range >}} becomes {{< var cost.after_lo >}}-{{< var cost.after_hi >}} a month. Data delivered inside AWS: high end {{< var cost.after_data_hi >}}
:::

## Assumptions to confirm

::: {.kicker}
AWS vs local
:::

::: {.rule}
:::

:::: {.grid-2}
::: {.card }
::: {.label .blue}
Science and operations
:::

- GPU hours per day, and GPU memory, for L2 → L3
- Which downloads really happen (L1 delivery, L0 archive copy, scientists pulling L2/L3), and how often
- How long L2 and L3 stay in AWS
- Which L3 planes are published: one merged file is ~{{< var cost.l3_gib >}} GiB a day
:::

::: {.card }
::: {.label .amber}
Engineering and money
:::

- AWS speed is unmeasured. Locally, 2 workers did 33.6 GB/h on the heavy placeholder, so one day takes about 12 hours on a fast desktop
- Discounts: Savings Plans for the always-on machines, or a research egress waiver?
- How L0 is packaged: about {{< var cost.l0_files >}} files a day drives request and archive costs
:::
::::

::: {.banner}
All numbers are AWS list prices from its price files (16-22 September 2026), for Oregon (us-west-2). N. California would cost {{< var cost.nc_pct >}} more
:::
